scenario.description: A maintenance manager must decide whether to authorize a servo retrofit on Press 5 during Saturday's maintenance window and finalize the production allocation, lockout controls, commissioning, and quality-release steps, with input from controls engineering, production planning, safety, and quality.

shared_context.S1: Press 5 has shown intermittent servo-drive alarms during the last two production weeks, and a replacement servo retrofit kit is available in the maintenance storeroom.
shared_context.S2: The regular Saturday maintenance window runs from 06:00 to 16:00, and Elena makes the binding decision on whether Press 5 is taken offline for the retrofit.
shared_context.S3: Press 2 is available on Saturday, but it is already scheduled for a separate job in the same general production period.
shared_context.S4: At the plant's routine maintenance-readiness review, Elena asks controls engineering, production planning, safety, and quality for relevant findings before finalizing the work order.
shared_context.S5: Plant policy requires a maintenance work order to include documented findings from controls engineering, production planning, safety, and quality before the work is approved.

PF1.text: Ravi confirmed in the controls bench test this morning that the retrofit requires exactly 2 hours for a controller-parameter backup and restoration followed by exactly 6 hours of controlled commissioning; he has not attached the bench-test note to the work order yet.

PF2.text: Monique confirmed the released schedule this morning: 480 housings are due for Monday shipment, Press 2 can make exactly 240 of them on Saturday, and the remaining exactly 240 must be assigned to Press 5 after the retrofit; she has not updated the shared schedule because the maintenance decision is still open.

PF3.text: Gareth's Saturday arc-flash review requires a documented lockout with zero-energy verification by two authorized employees and a 1.5-meter exclusion boundary around Press 5's electrical cabinet; he completed the review yesterday but has not entered it in the safety permit.

PF4.text: Sofia's customer control-plan review requires exactly 20 first-off housings from the retrofitted press to receive dimensional and torque checks, with the remaining production held until Quality approves those results; she received the revised control plan last night but has not linked it to the press work order.

acceptance_conditions: The Press 5 servo retrofit must be authorized.
If the retrofit is authorized, Press 5 must be scheduled for exactly 8 hours of downtime.
Exactly 240 housings must be assigned to Press 2 and exactly 240 housings to Press 5.
If the retrofit is authorized, the Press 5 lockout must include documented zero-energy verification.
If the retrofit is authorized, the electrical cabinet exclusion boundary must be exactly 1.5 meters.
If the retrofit is authorized, exactly 20 first-off housings must receive the required checks.
If the retrofit is authorized, production must remain on quality hold until Quality approval.
The controls bench-test finding must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The controls bench test changes Press 5 downtime from an unspecified retrofit duration to exactly 8 hours and establishes the exact duration that must be scheduled when the retrofit is authorized.
The released schedule changes the allocation to exactly 240 housings on Press 2 and exactly 240 housings on Press 5.
The arc-flash review changes the authorized retrofit safety plan to documented zero-energy verification and an exact 1.5-meter exclusion boundary.
The revised control plan changes the authorized retrofit release plan to exactly 20 checked first-off housings followed by mandatory Quality approval before remaining production can proceed.
